facts.statement: Rewasaurus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically from the Carnian to Norian ages, in the Tiki Formation of India.
facts.quote: It is known from the Late Triassic (Carnian to Norian age) Tiki Formation of India.

facts.statement: Rewasaurus was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Sulagna Sen and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Sulagna Sen and colleagues described Rewasaurus as a new genus and species of silesaurid dinosauriform.

facts.statement: The genus name Rewasaurus honors the Rewa Basin in Madhya Pradesh, India, where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name, Rewasaurus, refers to the Rewa Basin in Madhya Pradesh, India, from which the fossils were recovered.

facts.statement: The species name minori is derived from the Latin word for 'small'.
facts.quote: The specific name, minori, comes from the Latin word minor, meaning "small."

facts.statement: The holotype of Rewasaurus minori consists of an incomplete skull and an articulated lower jaw.
facts.quote: The Rewasaurus minori holotype material consists of an incomplete skull and articulated mandible (lower jaw).

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur with the accession code IITKGPR1191.
facts.quote: It is permanently accessioned at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur in West Bengal, India, under the code IITKGPR1191.

facts.statement: The genus Rewasaurus contains only one known species, Rewasaurus minori.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Rewasaurus minori, known from a partial skull.

facts.statement: Rewasaurus possessed a slender snout, heterodont teeth, and a toothless, pointed tip on its lower jaw.
facts.quote: Like other silesaurids, Rewasaurus has a relatively slender snout, heterodont dentition, and a toothless pointed tip of the dentary.

facts.statement: Rewasaurus is distinguished by its short upper dentition relative to the lower, a dentary tip nearly level with the tooth row, and at least five teeth in the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Rewasaurus can be distinguished from other silesaurids based on the upper dentition being relatively short compared to the lower dentition, the dentary tip lying nearly level with the rest of the tooth-bearing edge, and the premaxilla bearing at least five teeth.

facts.statement: The toothless tip of the lower jaw curves upward to a sharp point forming a 13-degree angle between the upper and lower edges.
facts.quote: The edentulous tip of the dentary curves slightly upward, narrowing to a sharp point with an angle of 13° between the upper and lower edges.

facts.statement: Rewasaurus is classified as a dinosauromorph allied with silesaurids, which may represent the earliest ornithischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Rewasaurus () is an extinct genus of dinosauromorph allied with taxa traditionally regarded as silesaurids (possibly the earliest ornithischian dinosaurs).

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis by Müller (2025) places Rewasaurus within Sulcimentisauria as the sister taxon to Diodorus.
facts.quote: The Müller (2025) matrix recovered silesaurids as a paraphyletic grade leading to traditional ornithischians, with Rewasaurus as a member of the Sulcimentisauria and the sister taxon to Diodorus.

facts.statement: The environment where Rewasaurus lived was likely semi-arid with seasonal floodplains and rainfall.
facts.quote: The climate during which the Tiki Formation was deposited is suggested to be semi-arid with seasonal floodplains and rainfall, based on palaeosols.

rejected.statement: Rewasaurus is a small silesaurid with a reconstructed skull length of approximately 7 centimeters.
rejected.quote: Rewasaurus is a small silesaurid, with a reconstructed skull length of ~7 cm.
